result.stdout:
gscript im — the IM index/linter (imindex) over the operator's memory PLANES

USAGE:
  gscript im lint   [--hub <path>] [--budget N] [--warn-pct N] [--deep] [--strict] [--verbose]
  gscript im digest [--hub <path>] [--budget N]

OPTIONS:
  --hub <path>       ANCHOR plane — decides which dir owns im.json and the localmd/ root
                     (default: CLAUDE.md beside gscript.json's localmdPath).
                     It anchors; im.json's "hubs" declares the full set.
  --budget N         line budget — applies ONLY when no im.json declares a plane set;
                     a declared plane always uses its own budget (default 450)
  --warn-pct N       warn when usage reaches N% of budget (default 90)
  --archived-root R  pre-relocation root to warn on (repeatable; also im.json archivedRoots)
                     im.json foreignRoots = roots owned by ANOTHER BODY: absent from this
                     disk BY DESIGN, so a reference resolves instead of erroring
  --deep             also stale-path-scan localmd/*.md beside the primary plane
  --strict           UNRESOLVED paths become errors (allowlist polarity: refuse by default)
  --verbose          list unresolved and uncheckable paths

MULTIPLE PLANES: <hubDir>\im.json { "hubs": [ { path, budget, label }, ... ] }.
Paths are relative to the primary plane's directory; each carries its OWN budget.
im.json is operator data — a memory layout is not something a public tree should hold.

UNRESOLVED vs UNCHECKABLE: unresolved = the text names something this linter cannot
place (fatal under --strict). Uncheckable = the linter cannot stat it from this host
(never fatal — a capability limit is not a content defect, and conflating them just
teaches people to drop --strict).

lint exits 1 on any error (budget overrun, stale C:\work path, broken `localmd/…` ref)
so it can gate a ceremony; archived-location references are warnings only.
